verified_correct:
I checked the calibration code against Eq. (hsc) with brute-force synthetic checks (/tmp/claude-0/audit2/check_hsc.py) and read-only diagnostics on the cached predictions in results/cache (other scripts in /tmp/claude-0/audit2/). Nothing was written to the repository and no experiment was run. The following are correct:

1. hsc_quantiles reproduces Eq. (hsc) exactly up to grid rounding. Synthetic test: 30 calibration and 6 target buildings, 5% missing scores, kappa in {0, 24, 168, inf}, uniform prior, LOBO with K=all via excl and with K=5 via exclude_self. Result: 0 mismatches. The grid radius is always at least the exact quantile and at most one grid step (0.57%) above it.

2. Own scores come only from stages before h. self_before is added after each stage's radius. GHCP updates own after the stage; QShrink uses a shifted cumulative count; TQA-B's decayed mean uses days before hi; ACI updates after the day's radius.

3. The "+1" point mass is correct: denominator kappa + n + 1 with level 1-alpha. kappa=0 gives the ceil((1-alpha)(n+1))-th own score, which is undefined until n >= 9 at alpha=0.1.

4. kappa=inf uses the prior only, with the finite-sample level ceil((1-alpha)(N+1))/N. N is the total prior score count: neighbours' totals, or totals with the held-out building excluded.

5. LOBO exclusion is correct when descriptors are finite. The K=all path subtracts the held-out CDF and count; the K-given path masks the diagonal; tune_aci uses tot - binc.

6. Stage bins {1}, {2}, {3}, {4..6}, {7..13}, {14..27}, {28..56} match STAGE_EDGES and stage_bin.

7. Interval construction is correct: the CQR band [qlo - q·s, qhi + q·s] covers exactly when e <= q, and the absolute-score band is symmetric. Raw-SCP is an exact order statistic. No inverted CQR intervals were observed, although 24-32% of HSC-CQR radii are negative. LightGBM quantile crossing affects at most 1.6e-4 of target hours.

8. ACI is correct: alpha_{h+1} = alpha_h + gamma·Σ_j(alpha - err_{h,j}) on valid hours, with err = 1{e > q}. The sign and daily batching match 05_setup.

9. normalized_IS equals the s-normalised Winkler score for both scores, including the CQR base width (qhi - qlo)/s. That base width is a constant in every tuning, so it does not affect any argmin.

10. The grid is conservative: cum_counts counts e <= grid[g] (searchsorted, side left), and the radius is the first grid point with F >= level. The 1e-6 tolerance is below one-score resolution for every pooled quantile (1/N >= 3.5e-6). Inside the mixture it can exceed one prior-score step at small kappa and late stages, but that is under 1e-6 in probability.

11. float32 and int16 counts are exact: at most 24 scores per stage and at most about 1.2e5 pooled, far below 2^24.

12. Self-CP and Self-CQR are kappa=0 with fallback to the stage-matched pooled radius; the only exception is the grid-cap case in finding 5.

13. The -stage, -kNN and -shrink ablations, for both scores, are re-tuned and remove only the named component. HSC simple, HSC-CQR simple and HSC-CQR (MLP) match 05_setup. GHCP-CQR and TQA-B-CQR implement their manuscript descriptions.

14. The main random-protocol runs have no NaN calibration descriptors. Effects of the empty-bin issue on their aggregate MACD, under-covered share and median IS are at most 0.001.

verified_big.title: A NaN calibration descriptor breaks kNN neighbour selection and the LOBO exclusion
verified_big.description:
neighbours() is not NaN-safe. It computes mu = z_cal.mean, sd = z_cal.std and plain squared distances, then argsort. descriptor() in src/preprocessing/features.py:137 returns NaN for the log-mean-load component when a building's whole history window is missing, because np.maximum(NaN, 1e-3) is NaN. When even one calibration building has a NaN descriptor at stage h, the mean and s.d. of that column become NaN, so every distance at that stage is NaN.

Two things then go wrong. (1) For targets, np.argsort returns storage order, so every target gets the same K neighbours: calibration indices 0..K-1, unrelated to similarity. (2) In LOBO tuning (exclude_self=True), the diagonal +inf sorts before NaN, so each pseudo-target's own building becomes its first neighbour. Its own stage-bin CDF, which contains the very scores being scored, enters its prior. This contradicts 04_method ('prior built from the remaining calibration buildings').

The uniform-prior variants (HSC simple, HSC-CQR simple, -kNN) are immune. The main random-protocol runs are unaffected: no calibration descriptor is NaN in BDG2 or UCI seeds 0-4, and the cross-dataset and robustness runs reuse those calibration sets.
verified_big.failure_scenario:
Toy check (/tmp/claude-0/audit2/nan_knn.py): with one NaN calibration descriptor, every target's neighbours become [0,1,2]. Every LOBO pseudo-target i gets [i,0,1], i.e. the self building is included.

Cached leave-site-out predictions show the problem in real data:
- lso2: calibration descriptors are NaN at stages 1-7, so all 155 targets use an arbitrary prior during the first week.
- lso2, NaN-safe neighbours (nanmean/nanstd, NaN distance set to +inf) versus current code: LOBO picks kappa 96 instead of 168 for HSC, and K 50 instead of 25 for HSC-CQR.
- lso2 HSC coverage on day 2: 0.810 (fixed) vs 0.876 (current).
- lso2 HSC-CQR coverage on day 3: 0.882 vs 0.939; under-covered share 0.084 vs 0.071; MACD 0.0208 vs 0.0199.
- lso0 (stage 1 affected): HSC coverage on day 1 is 0.794 vs 0.884. Selected K is 25 vs 50 for HSC and 25 vs 100 for HSC-CQR.

The effect on the leave-site-out results reported for kNN-based HSC variants (the 'improvements persisted for unseen sites' claim, generalisation table, stage curves) is arbitrary in direction. Folds 3-4 are not cached yet.
verified_big.suggested_fix: In neighbours(): standardise with np.nanmean/np.nanstd. Set NaN distances to +inf, so a building with an undefined descriptor (or no scores in B(h)) is never a neighbour. Apply exclude_self by masking the diagonal to a value strictly larger than every other entry, or by removing the index explicitly, rather than relying on inf versus NaN ordering. Add a unit test with one NaN calibration descriptor that asserts self is never selected and that the neighbour sets equal those computed without the NaN building. Then recompute the leave-site-out parts.

unverified_small.title: Calibration buildings with no scores in a stage bin enter the prior as all mass at +inf
unverified_small.description:
cal_cdf = cbc / max(tot,1) gives a building with zero valid scores in bin B a CDF that is 0 everywhere. prior_cdf then averages it (nbr path, line 123; uniform/LOBO path, lines 124-129) as if it were an empirical distribution, which amounts to placing that building's whole 1/K weight at +inf. Eq. (prior) averages EDFs, which are undefined for an empty bin. Such buildings exist in BDG2: 0-3 per seed in bins {1}, {2}, {3} or {4..6}, plus leave-site-out folds 0 and 1. UCI has none.

With small K, one such neighbour drops the maximum of F_prior to (K-1)/K. With K=10 and few own scores, the mixture then never reaches 1-alpha, and the radius becomes the INF_RADIUS cap (60·s). Pooled methods are unaffected, so the identity 'SCP-stage = HSC with kappa=inf, K=all' in 05_setup also breaks.
unverified_small.failure_scenario:
- BDG2 random s1: calibration building 7 has no scores in bin {4..6}. Target 55, which has it among its 25 nearest neighbours, gets HSC radius 60 at stages 5 and 6 instead of 1.35 and 1.25 when empties are excluded. That building's relative IS rises by 2.05.
- s0 HSC-CQR (K=100): radii are inflated in 398 (target, stage) cells across 208 of 253 targets, median ×1.43 at stages 2-3.
- lso1 (empty stage-1 bin): 22 LOBO pseudo-targets get radius 60 on day 1 at K=10. This inflates the K=10 tuning objective to 1.152 vs 0.931 (abs, kappa=168) and 0.636 vs 0.412 (CQR), so K=10 is ruled out by an artefact. Had K=10 been applied, 10 of 140 targets would get radius 60 on day 1 (median relative IS 0.635 vs 0.575).
- E7 sensitivity grid, s3 at K=10: 3-5 targets get radius 60 on day 1; mean relative IS 0.842 vs 0.821.
- In the main runs, MACD, under-covered share and median IS change by at most 0.001.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Average F_prior only over buildings with at least one score in B(h): use weights w_c = 1{tot_c,B > 0}, renormalise, and in the LOBO K=all path divide by the number of non-empty buildings excluding self. Alternatively, choose the K nearest among buildings that have scores in B(h). Add a unit test with an empty-bin calibration building.

unverified_small.title: The 'HSC fixed-kappa' ablation is identical to HSC in 6 of 10 main runs
unverified_small.description: The fixed-kappa variant reuses the jointly tuned K (nb) with kappa=168. Whenever LOBO already selects kappa=168, the variant removes nothing. Per-building results in results/parts confirm the outputs are identical for BDG2 s0, s1, s3, s4 and UCI s0, s4. It also exists only for the absolute-score HSC; there is no fixed-kappa variant of HSC-CQR, which is the headline method and usually tuned to kappa=336. In addition, K is not re-tuned given kappa=168, although the MS_ablation caption says 'Every variant is re-tuned'.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: 06_results states: 'Fixing κ at one week (168 h) instead of selecting it gives similar results, which indicates that the shrinkage does not hinge on fine-tuning.' For 4 of 5 BDG2 seeds and 2 of 5 UCI seeds, the compared methods are the same method (max |Δcov| = 0), so this ablation row largely compares HSC with itself.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Base the robustness-to-kappa claim on the E7 kappa sweep, or fix kappa at a pre-specified value for both scores, re-tune K given that kappa, and report how often fixed equals tuned. Otherwise drop or reword the sentence.

unverified_small.title: The 'HSC -kNN -stage' ablation is not re-tuned and duplicates 'HSC simple' with a different kappa
unverified_small.description: This variant uses b3['kappa'], the kappa tuned for the stage-matched '-kNN' variant, but evaluates with stage_matched=False. That contradicts the comment 'each re-tuned on calibration buildings with the component removed'. 'HSC simple' (line 354) is the same configuration (K=all, no stage matching) with kappa correctly re-tuned. The non-re-tuned variant is still in analysis.ABLATIONS, so it appears in the supplementary T_ablation tables and in the HSC ablation family of paired Wilcoxon tests.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: On BDG2, b3 kappa is 96, 96, 48, 48, 96 (seeds 0-4), taken from the stage-matched LOBO. The supplementary ablation tables and statistics.csv will report a '-kNN -stage' result next to 'HSC simple' for the same configuration but a different kappa. This misattributes the effect of removing both components, and the variant also affects the Holm family size.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Drop 'HSC -kNN -stage' (superseded by 'HSC simple') from run_calibration and from analysis.ABLATIONS, or re-tune it with tune_hsc(..., stage_matched=False, Ks=[None]).

unverified_small.title: The grid cap at 60 doubles as the infinity sentinel: anti-conservative radii and wrong Self-* fallback
unverified_small.description:
GRID[-1] = 60 = INF_RADIUS. cum_counts clips scores above 60 into the last grid point (calibration.py:55). A mixture quantile that truly exceeds 60 is therefore returned as 60 and used as a finite radius. That is anti-conservative relative to Eq. (hsc), contrary to 04_method's 'rounded upwards (conservatively)'.

The Self-CP and Self-CQR fallback test (q >= 0.999·INF_RADIUS, lines 291 and 333) and QShrink's 'defined' mask (calibration.py:242) cannot tell 'undefined, too few own scores' apart from 'defined but at least 60'. They substitute the pooled radius exactly when the building's own errors are extreme.
unverified_small.failure_scenario:
BDG2 random s1, target 55 (24 own scores above 60; 90% own-score quantile about 71-76 at stages 4-6):
- HSC returns 60 at stage 4 even with empty bins excluded, while Eq. (hsc) gives about 76.
- Self-CP and Self-CQR fall back to the pooled radius (about 0.2-0.3) in 8 stage-cells where n_own >= 9, so the own quantile is defined.
- QShrink sets w=0 in those cells.

Only this building is affected across the 10 main runs, so the impact is negligible.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Extend the grid upper limit or treat the tail exactly, and keep a separate +inf sentinel distinct from the largest finite grid point. Base the Self-*/QShrink fallback on n_own < ceil((1-alpha)(n_own+1)), not on the radius value. Document the cap in 04_method.

unverified_small.title: SCP-stage is not exactly 'HSC with kappa=inf, K=all' as 05_setup states
unverified_small.description: pooled_quantile weights every score equally (pooled counts). The kappa=inf branch of hsc_quantiles weights every building equally (mean of per-building CDFs) and applies the level ceil((1-alpha)(N+1))/N with N = total scores. The two coincide only when all calibration buildings have the same number of valid scores in a bin. test_hsc_limits passes only because its synthetic data has no missing values.
unverified_small.failure_scenario:
BDG2 s0:
- Absolute score, bin {3}: SCP-stage 0.2834 vs HSC(kappa=inf, K=all) 0.2949 (driven by the empty-bin building).
- Absolute score, bin {14..27}: 0.2159 vs 0.2147 (unequal counts only).
- CQR, bin {2}: 0.0085 vs 0.0127.
Comparisons of '-shrink' with SCP-stage are therefore not the pure one-component change the text implies.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Reword 05_setup to 'analogous to HSC with κ=∞, K=all (score-weighted rather than building-weighted)', or make the two definitions coincide. Add a missing-data case to test_hsc_limits.

unverified_small.title: The tuning objective is not Eq. (is) as 04_method states
unverified_small.description: 04_method says (κ, K) minimise 'the mean normalised interval score (Eq. [-@eq:is])'. Eq. (is) divides by the building's window mean ȳ_b and is computed per building. normalized_IS instead divides each hour's Winkler score by s_{b,h} and pools all calibration building-hours, so buildings with more valid hours carry more weight, and undefined radii enter as 60. The base-width term (zeros for the absolute score; (qhi-qlo)/s for CQR) is an additive constant with respect to κ, K, γ and λ. It never affects an argmin, so passing zeros in tune_aci for CQR scores is harmless.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: A reader reproducing the selection with per-building relative IS (Eq. is) would optimise a differently weighted objective and could select different (κ, K) when building scales drift within the window.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Describe the objective as 'the mean over all calibration building-hours of the interval score divided by s_{b,h}' and drop the Eq. (is) reference, or implement Eq. (is) if that is what was intended.

unverified_small.title: QShrink-CQR: lambda grid differs from the manuscript, and the tuning pooled quantile differs from the applied one
unverified_small.description: 05_setup says λ is selected 'from the same grid as κ', but lams = (24..1344) omits 0 and ∞. tune_qshrink's LOBO q_pool (line 232) is the building-weighted kappa=inf HSC quantile, which includes the empty-bin artefact above. The target application (line 345) uses the score-weighted pooled_quantile. Tuning and application therefore use different pooled radii.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: In BDG2 s0, the LOBO pooled radius differs from the applied pooled radius in bins {2} and {3} (e.g. CQR 0.0127 vs 0.0085). This can shift the selected λ for a baseline that is compared head-to-head with HSC-CQR.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Use the LOBO-excluded pooled counts (tot - binc per pseudo-target, as in tune_aci) for q_pool during tuning. Either state the actual λ grid or add 0 and ∞ to it.

unverified_small.title: ACI with alpha_h > 1 yields radius GRID[0] = -10, an inverted interval for the absolute score (latent)
unverified_small.description: When lev = 1 - a <= 0, idx is set to 0, so q = -10. For the absolute score this gives lo = yhat + 10s > hi = yhat - 10s: negative width, and the interval score is that of an inverted interval rather than Gibbs and Candès's empty set or zero-radius convention. The lev >= 1 case is handled as the 60·s cap.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: This needs α_h > 1, e.g. γ = 0.01 with about 38 or more consecutive fully covered days. It is not reachable with the γ values selected so far (0.0005-0.002: maximum drift 0.27 over 56 days), so there is no current impact. It could arise in other settings or with the top of the γ grid.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: For lev <= 0, use radius 0 for the absolute score (or an explicit empty-set convention) instead of GRID[0]. Document the conventions for the lev >= 1 and lev <= 0 cases.

verified_correct:
I read the code (calibration.py and pipeline.py as at HEAD cf165e6; the calibration functions are unchanged since 1ac1a38), compared it with the original papers, ran synthetic brute-force checks, and inspected cached predictions read-only (no interval methods were evaluated on targets). Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/audit2/.

1) Implementations match the stated specs exactly. In check_baselines.py, ghcp_quantiles, qshrink_quantiles and tqab_quantiles agree with independent brute-force versions of the specs to ≤2.4e-7. The test data had 30 calibration buildings, 6 targets, 56 stages, 5% missing scores and heterogeneous scales.
- GHCP: each reference building gets weight 1/(K+1) spread over all its scores. The new building's observed scores (stages < h only) each get 1/((K+1)·max(n_sur, n_own)); the rest of its share sits at +inf. n_sur is the median calibration count: 1344 in every checked cache, while the largest own count is 1320, so the +inf mass is always positive.
- QShrink: q_own is the ceil((1-α)(n+1))-th smallest own score from stages < h. w = n/(n+λ), where n is the number of own scores before the stage, and w = 0 while too few own scores exist. At deployment q_pool is the stage-matched CQR radius. In tune_qshrink, q_pool is the leave-one-building-out (LOBO), stage-matched pooled radius, and the IS objective and base width are the same as for HSC-CQR.
- TQA-B: the statistic is the decay-0.8 weighted mean of daily mean scores, normalised by the weight sum, using only days before the forecast. The rank uses strict '<' with denominator N+1 against the calibration buildings' statistics at the same stage. g^B uses C = α²/(1-α)², and a = clip(α-g, 0.01, 1). a = α at stage 1 or when the building has no own history. The level 1-a is taken on the count-weighted, stage-matched pooled CQR distribution.

2) Faithfulness to the papers.
- TQA-B: β=0.8, the rank formula, g^B and C match Lin et al. 2022. The clip versus the paper's λ-scaling and the missing +inf point are negligible.
- GHCP: the Eq. 5 weights match. The deviations (median rather than random donor, no floor(o/2) split, no N_j>o selection, no stage bins) are numerically negligible here. Omitting the group-mean local predictor most likely favours GHCP.
- QShrink: the q_g^reg = w·q_g + (1-w)·q_global form matches Rafe & Das. Tuning λ by LOBO is more favourable to QShrink than the paper's fixed λ=50.
- TQA-E: its update equals ACI's apart from the a>1 branch.

3) All CQR-based methods share the same base. CQR, HSC-CQR and its ablations, Self-CQR, ACI-CQR, GHCP-CQR, QShrink-CQR, TQA-B-CQR and HSC-CQR simple all use the same Scq/Stq scores, built from the same LightGBM qlo/qhi on calibration and target windows, and the same band(lo=PT.qlo, hi=PT.qhi). The MLP variants consistently use mqlo/mqhi on both sides. No quantile crossing occurs in the checked caches (qlo>qhi share = 0).

4) Tuning uses calibration buildings only.
- tune_hsc, tune_aci and tune_qshrink use only PC scores, with LOBO (self excluded) and the same pre-specified objective.
- GHCP's n_sur comes from calibration buildings, and TQA-B's β is fixed at the paper's value.
- No target information enters any selection, and the unused `fixed` path does not matter.
- The equal-weight LOBO pool in tune_qshrink differs from the count-weighted deployment radius by at most 0.005·s on BDG2 s0 and 0 on UCI s1 (lobo_real.py), which is negligible.

5) Evaluation plumbing. The new methods always give finite radii, so common_mask is unchanged. They are removed for α≠0.1. They are included in FAMILY_CQR for the Holm-adjusted tests.

6) Stage dependence of CQR scores is tiny: per-bin CQR radii are 0.006-0.019·s. So GHCP's lack of stage matching does not handicap it.

Overall: no adaptation materially biases the comparisons in favour of HSC. The only defect that favours HSC (the QShrink/Self-CQR grid-top fallback) affects one target building in 8 stages in the existing caches.

unverified_small.title: QShrink treats a legitimately huge own quantile (grid top) as 'undefined' and falls back to the pooled radius
unverified_small.description: qshrink_quantiles decides whether the own split-conformal quantile exists from its value: `defined = q_own < INF_RADIUS * 0.999`. cum_counts clips every score above GRID[-1]=60 into the last grid cell. A building can have plenty of own scores (so the quantile is defined) while its own (1-alpha)-quantile is at or above ~60·s. That building gets q_own = INF_RADIUS, so defined=False, w=0, and QShrink returns the pooled CQR radius (~0.01·s). This throws away the strongest own evidence the method could see. In the same hours HSC keeps a large radius, because its mixture reaches 1-alpha only near the grid top. The Self-CP/Self-CQR fallbacks (pipeline.py:291, :333) use the same value test, so the bug predates this change. Bias direction: in favour of HSC-CQR (and against QShrink-CQR and Self-CQR) on the affected buildings. Measured impact in the existing caches is negligible for medians and the paired Wilcoxon tests, but the mean rel. IS of that one building is inflated.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: Real data (cached predictions, diagnostic in /tmp/claude-0/audit2/count_top.py): one BDG2 seed-1 target building has 8 stages where its own CQR-score 90% quantile is at the grid top while the count is sufficient. There QShrink-CQR and Self-CQR revert to the pooled radius. One BDG2 seed-4 calibration building has the same in 2 stages, which feeds into the lambda LOBO tuning. Synthetic reproduction (/tmp/claude-0/audit2/qshrink_edge.py): own scores equal 80 for days 6-20. QShrink then returns -0.113, the pooled radius, at every stage from 11 to 56. The specified blend w*q_own+(1-w)*q_pool with lambda=168 would give about 0.59*60 ≈ 35 at stage 11, and HSC (kappa=168) gives 60.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Decide definedness from counts, not from the value: defined = np.ceil((1-alpha)*(n_own+1)) <= n_own, with n_own the number of observed own scores before the stage. When it is defined, keep q_own (even = INF_RADIUS) in the blend, or extend GRID's upper end. Apply the same count-based test to the Self-CP/Self-CQR fallbacks (pipeline.py:291 and :333).

unverified_small.title: QShrink lambda grid differs from the stated 'same grid as kappa' (no 0, no inf); tuning table discarded
unverified_small.description: tune_qshrink searches lams=(24,48,96,168,336,672,1344). manuscript/sections/05_setup.md:37 says lambda is selected 'from the same grid as kappa', i.e. {0,24,...,1344,inf}. So the text is factually wrong, and QShrink cannot reach its limits: lambda=inf is pooled CQR and lambda=0 is self-only with fallback. HSC-CQR's grid contains both limits, so the comparison is asymmetric. Any bias goes against QShrink and toward HSC. The tuning table is thrown away (`lam, _ = tune_qshrink(...)`, pipeline.py:343) and only lambda is logged, so a boundary hit cannot be detected from the outputs. HSC-CQR's kappa was interior (168/336) in all 10 existing main runs, so binding is unlikely in the main runs, though stress settings cannot be ruled out.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: Suppose the LOBO interval score keeps decreasing toward lambda=inf, e.g. noisy own scores in a stress test. Then tune_qshrink silently returns 1344, which puts weight w=0.5 on the noisy own quantile at day 56. That method is neither the LOBO optimum nor what 05_setup.md describes, while HSC-CQR in the same run may select kappa=inf.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Either tune over the same KAPPAS grid (map lambda=0 to self-only with fallback and lambda=inf to the CQR radius), or correct the manuscript text to {24,...,1344}. Store the tuning table (or a boundary-hit flag) in info for each part.

unverified_small.title: ACI-CQR gamma (now also presented as TQA-E) is selected at the lower edge of the grid in 7/10 runs
unverified_small.description: LOBO tuning of ACI-CQR uses only calibration buildings, which is correct, but the pre-registered grid binds. In the existing main alpha=0.1 parts, aci_cqr_gamma = 0.0005 = min(GAMMAS) in 7 of 10 runs (BDG2 s1-s4, UCI s1-s3; results/parts/main_*_a0.1_info.json). The ACI code is unchanged and the caches are reused, so the recomputation will select the same gamma. 05_setup.md:35 now says ACI-CQR also represents TQA-E. ACI-CQR may therefore be slightly under-tuned on the pre-specified IS objective, a small bias toward HSC-CQR. It is small because gamma->0 converges to CQR, which is reported separately.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: The LOBO objective is still decreasing at gamma=5e-4. ACI-CQR (as ACI-CQR and as the TQA-E stand-in) is then evaluated at a boundary value rather than at its optimum, and the paired tests compare HSC-CQR with an under-tuned competitor.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Report the boundary hits. As a logged deviation from the preregistration, consider extending GAMMAS downward (e.g. 1e-4, 2e-4) or adding gamma=0, and store the tuning tables.

unverified_small.title: TQA-B text says the clipping is 'as in the original method'; the paper scales g by lambda and adds a +inf point
unverified_small.description: Checked against Lin, Trivedi & Sun 2022 (arXiv:2205.09940, Sec. 4.2). These match the paper: beta=0.8; rank r = |{j: v_j < v_i}|/(N+1); g^B with C=alpha^2/(1-alpha)^2. These differ: (i) the paper sets delta=lambda*g(r) with lambda chosen so that a_t >= 0.01. This scales the whole budget function and keeps its zero mean. The code clips a=clip(alpha-g,0.01,1). (ii) The paper queries Q(1-a; scores ∪ {inf}). The code takes level 1-a of the pooled CDF with no +inf point. (iii) The paper normalises the decayed mean by t; the code uses the weight sum. That is rank-invariant without missing days and better with them. The effects are negligible. The clip binds only when r>0.99, i.e. only for the top-ranked building per stage when N>=111 (BDG2 N=168; never for UCI N=63), giving level 0.99 instead of about 0.994. The +inf point is worth <=1/N with N >= ~4,000 pooled hourly scores per bin. There is no material bias for or against HSC.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: BDG2, N=168: the top-ranked target at a stage has r=168/169, g=0.094, alpha-g=0.006, which is clipped to 0.01. The paper's lambda-scaling (lambda≈0.956) would instead shrink every building's adjustment by about 4%. So '05_setup.md:35 ... as in the original method' is inaccurate as written.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Reword 05_setup.md:35, e.g. 'a is clipped at 0.01 (the original rescales g so that a>=0.01) and the +inf point is omitted (negligible with thousands of pooled scores)', or implement the lambda-scaling.

unverified_small.title: GHCP-CQR: undocumented deviations from Mallick et al. Eq. 5 and the 'same stage bins' claim; K notation clash
unverified_small.description: I checked the code against the paper (arXiv:2608.15500, Eq. 5 and the donation/local-predictor steps). The code matches Eq. 5's structure: each reference building gets 1/(K+1) spread over its scores; the test group gets 1/(K+1) over its observed scores plus +inf mass. The undocumented differences are: (a) reference CDFs are pooled over all stages (bincq.sum(axis=1)). This contradicts 05_setup.md:21, 'All conformal-type methods share the same ... stage bins', and the GHCP description at :36 does not say so. (b) The code uses a deterministic median surrogate size; the paper draws a random donor J0~Unif{j: N_j>o} and removes it from S_cal. (c) The code uses all o own scores and all N_j reference scores; the paper sets aside floor(o/2) observations in every group. (d) The paper restricts to reference groups with N_j>o; the code does not. (e) In 05_setup.md:36, '1/(K+1)' uses K for the number of calibration buildings, while Section 4 uses K for the number of neighbours. All measured effects are negligible. On calibration CQR scores, the stage-agnostic radius covers 0.888-0.924 of each stage bin's scores (BDG2 s0, UCI s1; /tmp/claude-0/audit2/stage_effect.py). n_sur=1344 and the maximum own count is 1320 in every checked cache, so the +inf mass never vanishes. Differences in +inf mass are <=~1e-4. The documented omission of the local predictor most likely favours GHCP. In the paper that predictor is the group mean, shrunk with lambda=floor(o/2)/(|S_train|+floor(o/2)), where |S_train| is the number of training groups (~380 BDG2, ~140 UCI). Lambda would reach ~0.64/0.82 by day 56, mixing a constant building mean into the hourly forecast. Net effect: no bias in favour of HSC.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: A reviewer re-implements GHCP-CQR from 05_setup.md with stage-binned reference scores (as line 21 states) and a random donor, and gets a slightly different method. They also read '1/(K+1)' as K nearest neighbours.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: In 05_setup.md:36, state that the reference scores pool all onboarding stages, that the surrogate size is deterministic (median; all sizes ≈1344), that no floor(o/2) split is made because there is no local step, and the local-predictor rationale. Use a symbol other than K for the number of calibration buildings, and qualify line 21.

unverified_small.title: (Outside this dimension) A calibration building with an empty stage bin enters the prior as an all-zero CDF, i.e. +inf mass
unverified_small.description: hsc_quantiles builds cal_cdf = counts/max(tot,1). A building with tot=0 in a bin gets an identically-zero CDF, and prior_cdf still averages it into the kNN or uniform prior. This puts 1/K (or 1/(n-1)) of the prior mass at +inf. It also enters tune_qshrink's LOBO pool through hsc_quantiles(kappa=inf), where the effect is negligible (<=1/(n-1)). The effect works against HSC (conservative for the paper's claims) and can penalise small-K candidates in LOBO.
unverified_small.failure_scenario: BDG2 seed-0 cache: one calibration building has no valid CQR score in stage bins {2} and {3}, while its stage-2/3 descriptors are finite, so it can be chosen as a neighbour. For a target or LOBO pseudo-target that has it among K=10 neighbours at stages 2-3, FP_max=0.9. kappa=inf (the '-shrink' ablation) then gives the 60·s grid-top radius. Finite kappa inflates the radius to about the max of the own ~96th percentile and the prior's upper tail.
unverified_small.suggested_fix: Average only over neighbours or buildings with tot>0 in that bin (renormalise the weights), or substitute the building's adjacent-bin CDF.
